section: Migration - types, streams, causes and consequences; internal migration in India
subsections: Streams - rural-rural, rural-urban, urban-urban, urban-rural: shares and gender pattern
Causes - push and pull factors, reasons by gender

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the largest stream of internal migration in India?
o: Rural to rural
Urban to rural
Urban to urban
Rural to urban
accepted.x: Rural-to-rural migration is the largest stream of internal migration in India. It was also the stream contributing most to migration in 2011.
accepted.tq: Use the direct largest-share recall method and distinguish the dominant stream from urbanisation-linked migration.
accepted.sec: Streams - rural-rural, rural-urban, urban-urban, urban-rural: shares and gender pattern

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding rural-to-rural migration in India:
1. It has historically been dominant between agricultural areas.
2. It generally involves movement from low-potential to higher-potential farm areas.
3. It is predominantly female-dominated because of marriage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Rural-to-rural migration has historically linked agricultural areas, often from low-potential to higher-potential regions, and women form the dominant group mainly because of marriage.
accepted.tq: Test a cluster of related characteristics while using the all-inclusive coded option.
accepted.sec: Streams - rural-rural, rural-urban, urban-urban, urban-rural: shares and gender pattern

accepted.s: Rural-to-urban migration in India is generally characterised by which one of the following combinations?
o: Male movement for employment and growth of urbanisation
Female movement for marriage and declining urbanisation
International movement of skilled workers and suburbanisation
Retired persons moving to villages and rural rejuvenation
accepted.x: Rural-to-urban migration is dominated by males moving for employment and is an important force driving urbanisation.
accepted.tq: Separate the gender pattern and consequence of rural-to-urban migration from those of other streams.
accepted.sec: Streams - rural-rural, rural-urban, urban-urban, urban-rural: shares and gender pattern

accepted.s: Urban-to-urban migration is especially typical of which of the following countries mentioned in the context of migration streams?
o: India and Nepal
Brazil and Bangladesh
The USA and Japan
The Sahel countries and India
accepted.x: Urban-to-urban migration is identified as typical of developed countries such as the USA and Japan.
accepted.tq: Use the country-example association to distinguish developed-country urban migration patterns.
accepted.sec: Streams - rural-rural, rural-urban, urban-urban, urban-rural: shares and gender pattern

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the most appropriate description of urban-to-rural migration in India?
o: A small stream occurring in circumstances such as return migration or retirement
A stream dominated by inter-state male employment migration
The largest stream, caused mainly by marriage
A stream found exclusively in developed countries
accepted.x: Urban-to-rural migration is the smallest stream and occurs in special circumstances such as return migration and retirement.
accepted.tq: Find the precise exception-like description among statements referring to the four migration streams.
accepted.sec: Streams - rural-rural, rural-urban, urban-urban, urban-rural: shares and gender pattern

accepted.s: According to PLFS 2020-21, the overall migration rate in India was:
accepted.x: The overall migration rate recorded under PLFS 2020-21 was 28.9%.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the overall rate from the sex-specific and rural migration figures.
accepted.sec: Streams - rural-rural, rural-urban, urban-urban, urban-rural: shares and gender pattern

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the female migration pattern in PLFS 2020-21?
o: Female migration rate was 47.9%, and about 86.8% migrated for marriage
Female migration rate was 47.9%, and about 22.8% migrated for employment
Female migration rate was 28.9%, and 26.8% migrated for marriage
Female migration rate was 10.7%, and 22.8% migrated for marriage
accepted.x: The female migration rate was 47.9%, and approximately 86.8% of female migrants moved for marriage.
accepted.tq: Match the sex-specific rate with its principal stated reason and reject swapped percentages.
accepted.sec: Streams - rural-rural, rural-urban, urban-urban, urban-rural: shares and gender pattern

accepted.s: With reference to male migration in PLFS 2020-21, which one of the following is correct?
o: The male migration rate was 47.9%, and about 86.8% moved for employment.
The male migration rate was 26.8%, and about 10.7% moved for employment.
The male migration rate was 28.9%, and about 22.8% moved for marriage.
The male migration rate was 10.7%, and about 22.8% moved for employment.
accepted.x: The male migration rate was 10.7%, while about 22.8% of male migrants moved for employment.
accepted.tq: Apply a sex-and-purpose pairing rather than confusing male figures with female figures.
accepted.sec: Streams - rural-rural, rural-urban, urban-urban, urban-rural: shares and gender pattern

accepted.s: About what proportion of rural Indians were migrants in 2020-21?
accepted.x: About 26.8% of rural Indians were migrants in 2020-21.
accepted.tq: Identify the rural-specific proportion instead of the overall or sex-specific migration rates.
accepted.sec: Streams - rural-rural, rural-urban, urban-urban, urban-rural: shares and gender pattern

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the gender pattern in intra-state and inter-state migration?
o: Intra-state rural-to-urban migration is dominated by men, whereas inter-state rural-to-rural migration is dominated by women.
Intra-state rural-to-rural migration is dominated by women, whereas inter-state rural-to-urban migration is dominated by men.
Both intra-state and inter-state migration are dominated by women in urban-to-urban movements.
Both intra-state and inter-state migration are dominated by men in urban-to-rural movements.
accepted.x: Women dominate intra-state rural-to-rural movements, particularly those associated with marriage, while men dominate inter-state rural-to-urban movements for work.
accepted.tq: Contrast the territorial scale with the migration stream and gender pattern.
accepted.sec: Streams - rural-rural, rural-urban, urban-urban, urban-rural: shares and gender pattern

accepted.s: Among inter-state female migrants classified by place of last residence in 2011, which stream occupied the leading position in the stated migration pattern?
o: Rural-to-urban
Rural-to-rural
Urban-to-urban
Urban-to-rural
accepted.x: For inter-state female migrants by last residence in 2011, the migration pattern began with the urban-to-urban stream.
accepted.tq: Use the stated subgroup qualifier carefully instead of applying the general female rural-rural pattern.
accepted.sec: Streams - rural-rural, rural-urban, urban-urban, urban-rural: shares and gender pattern

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a PUSH factor for migration from rural areas?
o: Higher wages at the destination
Better transport access at the destination
Improved health care at the destination
Low farm productivity at the place of origin
accepted.x: Low farm productivity is a push factor operating at the area of origin. Higher wages, health care and transport access are pull factors of destinations.
accepted.tq: Apply the origin-versus-destination test to classify push and pull factors.
accepted.sec: Causes - push and pull factors, reasons by gender

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Poor rural infrastructure — Push factor
Monsoon failure — Push factor
Education — Pull factor
Political stability at origin — Push factor
accepted.x: Political instability, not political stability, is a push factor. Education is a pull factor, while monsoon failure and poor rural infrastructure push people away from the origin.
accepted.tq: Find the wrongly matched pair by separating adverse origin conditions from attractive destination conditions.
accepted.sec: Causes - push and pull factors, reasons by gender

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about rural-to-urban migration:
1. High labour demand in cities can encourage it.
2. Unbalanced rural-urban development can encourage it.
3. Lack of rural employment opportunities can encourage it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three conditions encourage rural-to-urban migration: cities generate labour demand, regional development is uneven, and rural areas may offer few employment opportunities.
accepted.tq: Recognise multiple simultaneous causes and select the comprehensive coded option.
accepted.sec: Causes - push and pull factors, reasons by gender

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the principal migration reasons by gender?
o: Women mainly migrate for marriage, while men mainly migrate for employment.
Women mainly migrate for employment, while men mainly migrate for marriage.
Both women and men mainly migrate for education only.
Both women and men mainly migrate because of retirement.
accepted.x: Women mainly migrate at marriage, whereas men mainly migrate for employment.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the two most easily reversed gender-wise migration reasons.
accepted.sec: Causes - push and pull factors, reasons by gender

accepted.s: About what proportion of India’s population is in the 10–24 age group, whose job search can contribute to rural-to-urban migration?
accepted.x: About 26% of India’s population is aged 10–24, and job search among this group can contribute to rural-to-urban migration.
accepted.tq: Link the age-group figure to its stated migration implication without confusing it with migration rates.
accepted.sec: Causes - push and pull factors, reasons by gender

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its role in migration?
o: Keralites and Sikhs — Information networks influencing migration
Drought in the Sahel — Pull factor of higher wages
Adulthood — Least mobile stage of life
Conflict — Destination amenity attracting migrants
accepted.x: Information networks associated with groups such as Keralites and Sikhs can influence migration. Adults are generally the most mobile, while drought and conflict are adverse conditions that push migration.
accepted.tq: Match examples with the type of factor or demographic influence they represent.
accepted.sec: Causes - push and pull factors, reasons by gender

accepted.s: Which one of the following environmental conditions is cited as a factor influencing migration?
o: Drought in the Sahel
Marriage in rural India
Urban transport access in Japan
Higher wages in Maharashtra
accepted.x: Drought in the Sahel is an example of an environmental factor influencing migration, generally by pushing people away from affected areas.
accepted.tq: Identify the environmental example while separating it from economic and social causes.
accepted.sec: Causes - push and pull factors, reasons by gender

accepted.s: According to Census 2011 data by place of last residence, the number of migrants in India was approximately:
o: 141.2 million
288.9 million
410 million
455.8 million
accepted.x: Census 2011 recorded 455.8 million migrants by place of last residence.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the total migrant stock from the subset that moved during 2001–11 and from inter-state migrants.
accepted.sec: Census D-series migration data - largest in- and out-migrating states

accepted.s: Of the 455.8 million migrants recorded by place of last residence in Census 2011, how many had moved during 2001–11?
o: 41.0 million
121.0 million
141.2 million
455.8 million
accepted.x: Among the 455.8 million migrants, 141.2 million had moved during the period 2001–11.
accepted.tq: Separate a period-specific migration figure from the total stock and the inter-state count.
accepted.sec: Census D-series migration data - largest in- and out-migrating states

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Census 2011 migration figures is correct?
o: There were exactly 1.4 crore inter-state migrants.
There were more than 4.1 crore inter-state migrants.
Inter-state migrants constituted all 455.8 million migrants.
There were fewer than 10 lakh inter-state migrants.
accepted.x: Census 2011 recorded more than 4.1 crore inter-state migrants. This was a subset of the total migrant population identified by place of last residence.
accepted.tq: Use scale discrimination to distinguish crore-based inter-state migration from the total migrant count.
accepted.sec: Census D-series migration data - largest in- and out-migrating states

accepted.s: Which one of the following states was among the leading source states of migrants according to the stated migration data?
o: Tamil Nadu
Kerala
Maharashtra
Uttar Pradesh
accepted.x: Uttar Pradesh and Bihar lead among source states for out-migration. Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Andhra Pradesh also send migrants.
accepted.tq: Distinguish source states from major destination states.
accepted.sec: Census D-series migration data - largest in- and out-migrating states

accepted.s: Which one of the following states was NOT included among the major destination states in the stated migration data?
o: Gujarat
Maharashtra
Karnataka
Bihar
accepted.x: Bihar is a leading source state, not one of the listed major destination states. Maharashtra, Gujarat and Karnataka are among the major destination states.
accepted.tq: Find the source-state intruder in a list of major destination states.
accepted.sec: Census D-series migration data - largest in- and out-migrating states

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct order of the leading out-migration states mentioned in the data?
o: Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, followed by Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh
Maharashtra and Delhi, followed by Gujarat and Haryana
Kerala and Andhra Pradesh, followed by Tamil Nadu and Gujarat
Punjab and West Bengal, followed by Delhi and Maharashtra
accepted.x: Uttar Pradesh and Bihar are the leading out-migration states, followed by states including Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan. The other options mainly describe destination states or reverse the source-state pattern.
accepted.tq: Start with the leading pair and distinguish source-state ordering from destination-state lists.
accepted.sec: Census D-series migration data - largest in- and out-migrating states

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the leading in-migration destinations listed in the migration data?
o: Delhi, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Odisha
Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh
Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Punjab
accepted.x: The listed leading in-migration destinations include Delhi, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala.
accepted.tq: Recall the destination-state cluster and avoid mixing it with the source-state cluster.
accepted.sec: Census D-series migration data - largest in- and out-migrating states

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs of migration lists is correctly arranged as source states followed by destination states?
o: Maharashtra and Gujarat; Uttar Pradesh and Bihar
Uttar Pradesh and Bihar; Maharashtra and Delhi
Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh; Bihar and Jharkhand
Delhi and Kerala; Rajasthan and Odisha
accepted.x: Uttar Pradesh and Bihar are leading source states, while Maharashtra and Delhi are major destination states.
accepted.tq: Compare the direction of migration and reject reversed source-destination pairs.
accepted.sec: Census D-series migration data - largest in- and out-migrating states

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly associates a future migration data source with its stated period or event?
o: Census 2027 — migration will not be recorded
NSO Nationwide Migration Survey — January 2020 to December 2020
Census 2011 — migration was first recorded in 2027
NSO Nationwide Migration Survey — July 2026 to June 2027
accepted.x: The NSO Nationwide Migration Survey is scheduled for July 2026–June 2027. Census 2027 is also stated to record migration.
accepted.tq: Match the institution and survey period while using the explicit negative trap about Census 2027.
accepted.sec: Census D-series migration data - largest in- and out-migrating states

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the relationship between the 455.8 million migrants and India’s population in Census 2011?
o: They constituted about 37.6% of a population of 121 crore.
They constituted about 47.9% of a population of 455.8 crore.
They constituted about 10.7% of a population of 47.9 crore.
They constituted about 26.8% of a population of 121 crore.
accepted.x: The 455.8 million migrants represented about 37.6% of India’s population of 121 crore in the stated Census 2011 comparison.
accepted.tq: Connect the numerator, percentage and population base instead of treating the figures as separate facts.
accepted.sec: Census D-series migration data - largest in- and out-migrating states
